audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition denominator and balance sheet are paired with pre-acquisition owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Brazos purchase price $1.672245 billion, including $820.3 million cash and 19.389239 million issued common units; Aris consideration included 26.6 million issued common units, while only $116.4 million of Aris revenue was consolidated in 2025; owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation divides FY2025 owner earnings, containing only post-October 15 Aris results and no Brazos results, by a post-Brazos unit count and combines it with a post-Brazos bridge; omitted acquired earnings understate value, while omitted acquisition financing interest and recurring integration costs overstate value.
audit_findings.evidence: Results of operations attributable to the Aris acquisition were included in the Partnership’s consolidated statements of operations beginning on the acquisition date in the fourth quarter of 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future change. The denominator and bridge reflect material acquisition consideration and financing for businesses whose corresponding recurring owner earnings are absent or only partially present. The competing earnings, financing, and dilution effects prevent a reliable direction from being established, but their scale is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on one consistent perimeter: either use FY2025 units and bridge with a documented Aris normalization, or construct post-closing owner earnings including full-period Aris and Brazos operations, maintenance capital, financing interest, recurring integration costs, the post-closing bridge, and the corresponding fully diluted claims.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method investments may be counted both in owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 equity income $85.788 million; 2025 equity-investment distributions $122.364 million; stakes_net bridge addition $493.5 million; distributions equal 11.24% of the $1,088.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If equity-investment income or distributions remain in owner earnings, their cash flows are capitalized in operating value while the same investments are also added through stakes_net in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Equity income, net – related parties decreased by $26.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily due to decreases of $7.6 million and $7.0 million at TEP and Mi Vida, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is not demonstrated because the anchor's line-item construction was not supplied. The possible exposure is nevertheless material: filed annual distributions equal 11.24% of the anchor, and a separate $493.5 million stake value is added to the bridge. If both treatments apply to the same investments, value is overstated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1,088.2 million anchor to the cash-flow statement and each investee. Identify the $90.973 million of distributions from earnings and $31.391 million of distributions exceeding cumulative earnings, remove all cash flows attributable to investments included in stakes_net, and rerun; alternatively retain those cash flows and remove the corresponding stake values.

audit_findings.title: The 9.1 million general-partner units may be missing from the claim denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: 9.060641 million units, equal to 2.17% of the stated 416.897647 million denominator; adding them produces 425.958288 million claims and reduces base value from $38.11 to approximately $37.30 per unit and bull value from $42.39 to approximately $41.49
audit_findings.mechanism: If the owner-earnings numerator includes the general partner's economic allocation, omitting its units understates total claims and overstates per-unit value.
audit_findings.evidence: We also have 9,060,641 general partner units issued and outstanding; there is no established public trading market for any such general partner units.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether an error exists remains unresolved because the record does not show whether owner earnings were reduced for the general partner allocation. Even assuming the full 9.060641 million units must be added, the approximately 2.1% reduction leaves the bull value about $8.05 below the $49.54 market price and does not alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify that every historical owner-earnings numerator excludes the general partner allocation. If not, add the 9.060641 million units or deduct the equivalent economic claim and update the reported per-unit values.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash obligations may be absent from both owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Expected settlements of $9.9 million in 2026 and $427.9 million thereafter; ARO carrying amount $437.8 million at 2025-12-31 and $471.748 million at 2026-06-30; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If maintenance capital does not include abandonment settlements while depreciation and ARO accretion are added back, future retirement cash outflows are omitted from owner earnings and no compensating liability is deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we expect to incur asset retirement costs of $9.9 million in 2026, and a total of $427.9 million in years thereafter.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash obligation and recorded liability are demonstrated, but omission from the valuation is not: the record does not disclose whether the maintenance-capital calculation already includes expected settlements. Settlement timing and overlap with maintenance capital are also unavailable, so materiality cannot be established without risking double counting.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the owner-earnings maintenance-capital schedule and the undiscounted ARO settlement schedule by year and asset. If settlements are excluded, model the cash flows or deduct an appropriately valued ARO claim, then rerun while removing any duplicated maintenance-capital allowance.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may retain unusually large acquisition expenses
audit_findings.magnitude: $120.5 million of 2025 acquisition-related G&A, comprising $104.6 million of severance and $15.9 million of consulting and legal fees; equal to 11.07% of the $1,088.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained nonrecurring acquisition costs depress the owner-earnings anchor and understate operating value; excluding costs that recur under WES's stated systematic-acquisition strategy would overstate sustainable owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, General and administrative expenses in the consolidated statements of operations include acquisition-related transaction costs consisting primarily of $104.6 million of severance costs and $15.9 million of third-party consulting and legal fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The expenses and their scale are demonstrated, but their treatment in the anchor is unresolved. At 11.07% of anchor owner earnings, normalization could materially change the valuation. Direction is mixed because full retention may be overly conservative, while full removal may ignore economically recurring acquisition and integration spending.
audit_findings.action: Trace all $120.5 million through the owner-earnings reconciliation, separating cash severance, non-cash compensation, transaction fees, integration costs, and recurring acquisition overhead. Rerun using only the portion supported as genuinely nonrecurring, with a separate recurring allowance for systematic acquisition activity.

audit_findings.title: Not all consolidated cash belongs to common unitholders
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum indicated exposure $26.1915 million, calculated as 25% of the entire $104.766 million cash bridge; approximately $0.063 per diluted unit and 0.16% of the $15.888 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Chipeta cash attributable to its 25% noncontrolling member is consolidated in cash but is not an asset of WES common unitholders; adding it to the bridge overstates common-equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, we are required to distribute a portion of Chipeta’s cash balances, which are included in the cash balances in our consolidated balance sheets, to the other Chipeta member.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that some consolidated Chipeta cash must be distributed to the other member, but does not state the amount. Even the conservative upper bound that all $104.766 million of consolidated cash belonged to Chipeta would reduce value by only about $0.063 per diluted unit, far too small to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 legal-entity cash ledger, identify Chipeta and other restricted or customer-funded balances, and exclude the non-common portion from the bridge; update the bridge without changing operating assumptions.
